title: Log warehouse archival and rehydration notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc captures design decisions, operational notes, and runbook fragments for Redwood's audit log archival and rehydration pipeline. Goal: ensure durable, searchable audit logs that meet compliance retention windows while keeping production indexes performant and cost-efficient. Covers event classification, storage tiers, indexing strategy, SIEM export considerations, backfill approaches, and failure-mode mitigations.

Context / constraints
- Primary consumers: security investigations, compliance evidence requests (SOC2, GDPR), SRE/debugging, and SIEM.
- Current infra: real-time audit events flow into Kafka topics (audit.events.v1), processed by stream processors, indexed into OpenSearch cluster for fast queries, and mirrored to GCS as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) in hourly partitions.
- BigQuery house-keeping: daily partitioned tables exist for aggregated queries, but not all raw fields are currently populated.
- Cost target: aging out hot indexes older than 30d to reduce Opensearch cluster size; keep raw archived copies for up to 7 years (compliance upper bound).

Event classification and retention buckets
- High-sensitivity (authz/authn failures, token issuance/revocation, admin role changes): hot index 90 days, warm store 1 year, cold archive 7 years.
- Medium-sensitivity (config changes, policy modifications, service account lifecycle): hot 60 days, warm 1 year, cold archive 3 years.
- Low-sensitivity (read-only resource access logs, metrics-level auditing): hot 30 days, warm 90 days, cold archive 1 year.
- SIEM export subset: all high-sensitivity + sampled medium-sensitivity for 365 days; exported daily into SIEM S3 bucket (prefix: siem-exports/YYYY-MM-DD).

Storage tiers and backends
- Hot (fast search): OpenSearch (primary cluster), using daily indices with rollover at 50GB. Retention policy enforces delete by index age/size via curator jobs.
- Warm (inexpensive retained index): OpenSearch warm nodes with slower storage for months 1..N depending on event class.
- Raw archive (cold, canonical): GCS bucket gs://redwood-audit-raw/ with path structure audit=events/v1/date=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/*.ndjson. Files are written by stream sink with md5 and manifest entries. Parquet conversion job runs weekly to produce columnar, compressed storage for BigQuery loads.
- Analytical store: BigQuery daily tables (partitioned by day) containing a filtered + normalized subset used for long-range queries and compliance reports.
- SIEM landing: S3 (external tenant) mirroring from GCS via transfer service; files are gzipped ndjson with manifest.

Indexing strategy
- Nearline: pipeline enriches each event with canonical resource ids, tenant id, and rbactags. Index mapping is intentionally sparse: frequently queried keys (actor_id, action, resource_type, timestamp, success) are top-level fields. Large free-form payloads are stored only in raw archive and in a keyword field truncated in OpenSearch to 2048 chars.
- Tokenization: use keyword fields for exact match (e.g., event_id, tenant) and text+ngram for message fields used in fuzzy search.
- Secondary indexes: daily aggregated indices for counts and anomaly detection (per-tenant activity summary).
- Reindexing plan: when we change mappings, run reindex from raw Parquet backed by a distributed reindex job (k8s job reading GCS ranges) that writes new indices directly to OpenSearch to avoid double-hop through Kafka.

Backfill and rehydration approaches
- Use-case: indices deleted/rotated or mapping change requiring reindex of historical data.
- Sources for backfill: raw ndjson in GCS; weekly Parquet; BigQuery export (as a fallback).
- Strategy 1 (preferred): streaming rehydrate job that streams ndjson from GCS, applies enrichment functions (same code path as producer), then bulk-indexs to OpenSearch using controlled concurrency. Job is checkpointed by file path + byte offset in a sidecar manifest to support resume.
- Strategy 2 (for massive reindex): convert parquet -> ES bulk files (partitioned by target index shard key) and use OpenSearch bulk importer (faster but needs careful shard targeting).
- Cost control: run reindex jobs on dedicated ephemeral clusters during maintenance windows and throttle write QPS to avoid overwhelming nodes.

Failure modes and mitigations
1) GCS files missing/corrupt
   - Symptom: rehydrate job fails on parse, md5 mismatch, or missing file error.
   - Mitigation: manifest contains checksums + file size. On parse error: move offending file to gs://redwood-audit-raw-quarantine/YYYY-MM-DD/ and create Jira ticket with file path + sample. If missing, check Kafka DLQ -> maybe data never persisted; escalate to stream-producer team.
2) OpenSearch bulk rejections / backpressure
   - Symptom: 429s or queue full, slow writes
   - Mitigation: exponential backoff + circuit breaker. Maintain monitoring on bulk queue length and set autoscaling triggers for warm nodes. If repeated, reduce bulk batch size and increase job parallelism count or defer to warm period.
3) Schema mismatch during reindex
   - Symptom: mapping conflict errors on _type or field with different data types.
   - Mitigation: implement a type-agnostic ingest transformation that coerces types; pre-run a small dry-run job to detect conflicts and create new index with compatible mapping before bulk indexing. Use reindex-from-source to avoid conflicts when possible.
4) SIEM export failures (transfer aborted / missing manifests)
   - Symptom: SIEM partner complains, transfer logs show 403/timeout.
   - Mitigation: automatic retry scheduling; fall back to creating signed temporary S3 staging for partner to pull. Send detailed failure notification to SOC on-call.
5) Backfill takes too long / cost overruns
   - Mitigation: stop job, evaluate cardinality of target ranges, increase sharding for bulk import path, or prioritize rehydration by tenant or time window. Maintain cost caps in k8s job spec to auto-cancel if compute spend > threshold.

Observability and alerts
- Metrics to instrument: file write success rate (to GCS), ndjson parse errors, bulk ES error rate, avg ES bulk latency, cursor lag for rehydrate jobs, SIEM export success rate, manifest vs. actual file count.
- Dashboards: compliance-retention (percent of events older than retention with archived copy), rehydrate-progress (bytes processed, files remaining), siem-transfer-health.
- Alerts: bulk-error-rate > 5% for 15m, GCS ingest failures spike > 1% of hourly files, rehydrate job stuck > 4h without progress, SIEM transfer failure for 3 consecutive days. Pager duty: security-oncall + infra-oncall.

Runbook fragments (for ops)
- Kick off a small dry-run reindex for 2024-02-01: 
  1) k8s job create --image registry/redwood/reindex:prod --env START_DATE=2024-02-01 --DAYS=1 --BATCH_SIZE=500 --CONCURRENCY=6
  2) monitor logs: kubectl logs -f job/reindex-20240201 | grep -E "ERROR|WARN"
  3) if mapping conflicts observed: create new index manual mapping: curl -XPUT es/_newindex -d '@mappings.json' and rerun job with TARGET_INDEX=_newindex

- Quarantine flow: if ndjson file corruption detected: gsutil mv gs://redwood-audit-raw/path gs://redwood-audit-raw-quarantine/path && create ticket JIRA:SEC-ARCHIVE-QUARANTINE with description and sample lines.

Compliance mapping and evidence packaging
- For SOC2 evidence requests: provide a manifest of index snapshots + signed GCS objects for the requested date range. Use the canonical Parquet export as primary evidence and include the transient OpenSearch query results for convenience.
- For GDPR deletion requests: canonical deletion must remove both OpenSearch docs and mark records in archive manifest with deletion markers; actual raw files are immutable but annotated. Deletion pipeline adds tombstones to BigQuery and creates a redaction task to strip PII on a copy for the archive-retention policy.

Open action items
- [ ] Finalize retention table with legal (Asha) by 2024-03-20.
- [ ] Implement manifest checksums and quarantine flow (Diego) - backlog SEC-4123.
- [ ] Add dry-run reindex automation in CI for mapping changes (Imani).
- [ ] Document SIEM transfer SLA and escalation matrix (Ethan) by next week.

References and links
- Confluence spec: CONFLUENCE:SEC-AUDIT-ARCHIVE-PLAN
- Jira epic: JIRA:SEC-4123
- Reindex job PR: GITHUB:github.com/redwood-inference/log-pipelines/pull/87

Notes / brainstorming (informal)
- Consider introducing an intermediate "rehydration cache" (short-lived Bigtable) for very fast lookups for recent months instead of keeping a large warm OpenSearch footprint.
- Could reduce index size by removing long payloads and storing just ids + pointer to raw archive; but that worsens investigator UX. Need to weigh operational cost vs mean time to resolution.

Timeline (high-level)
- Week 1: finalize retention buckets, add manifest checksums.
- Week 2-3: implement quarantine + SIEM retry logic.
- Week 4: run full dry-run reindex for 90d window and analyze cost.
- Month 2: flip retention enforcement to auto-delete hot indices > configured window, monitor customer impact.

If you are running a rehydrate/backfill or found a corrupted raw file, add notes here before escalating so we have an audit trail.

-- end of notes --
